The principle behind trypan blue staining is based on the concept of membrane integrity. Live cells have intact membranes that prevent the dye from entering the cytoplasm, while dead cells have damaged membranes that allow the dye to penetrate and stain the cells blue.

Therefore, if 25% of cells are stained blue with trypan blue, it means that 25% of the cells in the sample are dead.
